title: Drummers: Red Happy, Black Benny, Henry Martin

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And who were some of the good drummers in those days?
Little Happy, you know. Chinese.
Which Happy now? We gotta get to...
Red Happy. I don't know his last name. We used to call him Red Happy.
Well, that's good enough. There's so many Happys.
And Little Chinese. Black Benny was kind of rated up there among them, too.
For what? For bass snare?
Well, I mean, he played traps and bass drum, but he's the best on bass drum. But, I mean, he played traps, too, pretty nice. And this Martin fellow, what's his name?
Henry Martin.
Henry Martin.
Albert Henry, I forget. Just a couple of Martin guys. Which one was this, the one?
The drummer, Henry Martin.
And who did he work with?
He worked with Maple Leaf or something kind of leaf band or something.
It wasn't Fats, Martin. No, no, no. Fats was another.
He was named Henry Martin. He worked mostly, though, with the Silver Leaf or the Maple Leaf or something or another.
I see. And who'd be good on snare on the street?
Snare?
On the snare drum. On the street.

Them times? Mm-hmm. I'll tell you. Henry Martin was one of the best. Mm-hmm. Well, Happy, I don't believe I've never seen him play. Yeah, I did see him play parade. He played parade with us once. Long time ago. He played nice. I had Black Benny on the bass drum. He's the bad man on the bass drum. Boy, he played more bass drum. Sure.
